title: Unify reranker inputs and paged structured responses
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Problem summary: Customers using embeddings + reranking endpoints have inconsistent behavior when requesting top-k results across two axes: (1) ambiguous top_k semantics when scores tie or when input order is meaningful, (2) fragmented input schema differences between the embeddings+rerank API and legacy /search endpoints, and (3) poor ergonomics for paginating ranked results with deterministic continuation tokens. Additionally, structured output for each candidate (metadata, provenance, per-token traces) is not consistently returned or is expensive to compute for large candidate pools. This ticket proposes an ergonomic, backward-compatible input schema and paginated structured output model that improves quality (stable ordering and provenance), latency (early streaming of top results, lazy retrieval of heavy metadata), and scale (cursor-friendly pagination and batched score computation).
proposal: We will introduce a single canonical rerank request schema and response shape that supports the following: 1) explicit 'top_k' meaning (two modes: TOP_K_EXACT and TOP_K_AT_LEAST). TOP_K_EXACT returns exactly k items selecting tie-break by stable input-order fallback; TOP_K_AT_LEAST returns >=k items when score ties occur to avoid nondeterministic truncation. 2) a compact candidate representation for the hot path (id, score) and an optional 'details' flag to expand structured output (text_snippet, provenance, token_trace). 3) cursor-based pagination where cursors are opaque, stable across model-variant fallbacks, and include a checksum to detect drift. 4) streaming-first response: return initial compact top-k results as soon as scores for them are stable; stream expanded details as they become available. 5) backwards-compatible compatibility layer that maps existing top_k semantics to the new enum (default maps to TOP_K_EXACT).
api_examples:
Example request (compact):
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "Find relevant docs about credit card fraud",
  "candidates": [ { "id": "doc:123" }, { "id": "doc:456" } ],
  "top_k_mode": "TOP_K_EXACT",
  "top_k": 5,
  "details": false,
  "page_size": 100
}

Cursor-based follow-up to fetch expanded details: 
POST /v1/rerank?page_token=eyJ2IjoiMiIsImNoZCI6IjE2MjMifQ==
{ "details": true, "page_size": 20 }

Response (compact):
{
  "items": [ { "id": "doc:456", "score": 0.982 }, { "id": "doc:123", "score": 0.879 } ],
  "next_page_token": "...",
  "model_version": "reranker-v2.1"
}

Expanded item structure when details=true:
{ "id": "doc:456", "score": 0.982, "snippet": "...", "provenance": { "source": "kb-2", "offsets": [[120,240]] }, "token_trace": "(omitted unless requested)" }
acceptance_criteria: Canonical rerank request/response schema documented in the API spec and included in SDKs
Default behavior preserves existing customers' results (compat layer mapping verified by unit tests + sampling checks)
Cursor format is opaque, includes checksum to detect candidate set mismatch, and returns 410/RETRY_HINT if cursor invalid
TOP_K_EXACT and TOP_K_AT_LEAST semantics validated with unit+integration tests covering score ties and deterministic ordering
Streaming-first path returns compact top results with 95th percentile latency improvement in our synthetic end-to-end benchmark
Optional details expansion does not increase p95 on compact-only path beyond 5%
Migration guide and SDK patches published; deprecation notice for old endpoints if applicable
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement server-side schema and compatibility mapping behind feature flag; release internal SDK patch (python/node) that prefers new schema when available. Run canary against 5% of traffic with traffic shadowing to compare outputs. Phase 2: Enable streaming-first for canary; collect latency/quality metrics and customer telemetry. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with migrations notes for customers who use raw candidate texts. Phase 4: Deprecate old param names after 90 days of stable rollout and notify clients via console emails and API logs.
test_plan: Unit tests for top_k tie-break behavior, cursor round-trip tests, and schema validation. Integration tests against reranker runtime covering compact path, details expansion, and streaming. Performance tests: microbenchmarks to measure p50/p95 latency for compact-only vs details=true; load test simulating 10k candidates with page_size 100. Add fuzzing for malformed cursors and candidate checksum mismatches.
notes: Trade-offs considered: returning >=k to handle ties preserves recall but can change client-side paging expectations; therefore we give explicit mode selection.

Cursor stability across model rollouts implemented by anchoring cursor to canonical candidate ids + model-compatible hash; if model variant incompatible, API returns RETRY_WITH_FAULT explaining unsafe continuation.
Lazy details: store heavy metadata (token_trace) in a hot cache keyed by candidate id to avoid recomputation when details=true is requested after initial compact response.
We considered offset-based pagination but chose opaque cursors to allow internal reordering and cross-model fallbacks without exposing internal indexes.
Backwards-compat mapping table: old_param top_k -> top_k_mode=TOP_K_EXACT unless clients specify "allow_ties=true" which maps to TOP_K_AT_LEAST.
